question: Name one feature added in the latest Autodesk Fusion update.
answer:
Based on Autodesk Fusion's October 2026 release (build v.2706.1.17, October 28, 2026) [1], one new feature is Auto Timeline, which uses AI-assisted feature reconstruction to turn imported, non-native geometry into an editable parametric Fusion design [3]. It currently reconstructs extrudes, revolves, chamfers, fillets, holes and basic sweeps [3].

Other additions in the same release include System Modeler, a no-code, node-based automation tool found in the Automation tab of the Design and Manufacture workspaces [5], and built-in task management [3]. Note that v.2706.1.17 itself is a minor update with stability fixes, and the new features arrived with the October major update (v.2706.1.14, October 21, 2026) [1].

keyPoints.text: The October 2026 Fusion update adds AI-assisted Auto Timeline, which converts imported non-native geometry into an editable parametric design.
The October 2026 update adds System Modeler, a node-based visual automation environment for design and manufacturing tasks without code.
The October 2026 update adds built-in task management with Kanban or list views inside Fusion.
The October 2026 update adds eCAD drill views, drill tables and copper views in the drawings toolbar.
The most recent minor build is v.2706.1.17, dated October 28, 2026, which contains stability fixes only.

mayBeStale.text: The sources do not describe a November 2026 major update, so the October 2026 release is the latest major update found; a newer release may exist beyond these sources.
System Modeler is noted as requiring access to the Fusion Manufacturing Extension, so availability depends on the user's license.
Copy Designs Across Fusion Hubs is a staged rollout over two weeks, so it may not yet be available to all users.
Source 4 (dated 2026-10-28) is a generic support page with no release details, so it does not confirm the current version.
